proposal.hypothesis: Packing each B reduction-by-column panel into compact scratch may improve panel locality while it is reused across the 32x64 output tile, enough to offset the packing and allocation cost. Keeping the parent’s tile sizes, loop order, serial execution, first-reduction overwrite, and scalar 4x4 microkernel otherwise unchanged makes this a packing-focused comparison; the result remains unmeasured.

retained: Retain the selected parent’s 32x64 output tiles, 64-element reduction blocks, scalar register-oriented 4x4 microkernel, and serial tile traversal.
Allocate a 64x64 B-panel scratch buffer inside run and pack each current B panel before computing its corresponding output tile, so allocation and copying remain in timed cost.
Read packed B values in both the 4x4 microkernel and the fringe path; preserve first-reduction-block zero initialization so every output is overwritten on each call.
